chapters.summary: Committee staff opens the New York City Council Committee on Health vote, asks attendees to silence devices and not approach the dais, and tells the Chair the committee is ready to begin. No substantive business is discussed.
chapters.title: Committee staff opens Health Committee vote and calls meeting to order

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, good morning, and welcome to today's New York City Council vote from the Committee on Health.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, I'd like to remind everyone to kindly silence your electronic devices, and at no point is anyone to approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we are ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Lynn Schulman introduces herself and welcomes attendees to the vote on two bills and three resolutions focused on reproductive and maternal health. She frames the meeting as a committee action on a package of reproductive health measures.
chapters.title: Chair Schulman opens vote on reproductive and maternal health bills

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Lynn Schulman, Chair of the New York City Council's Committee on Health.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you all for joining us for today's vote on two bills and three resolutions focused on reproductive and maternal health.

chapters.summary: Schulman says New York City is a beacon for comprehensive, high-quality reproductive health care while the federal government and other states roll back bodily autonomy. She argues that anyone, regardless of identity, origin, or income, should receive nonjudgmental care, and says the legislation builds on that foundation.
chapters.title: Schulman frames NYC as beacon for reproductive health access

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: New York City is a beacon in the United States and across the globe for comprehensive access to high-quality reproductive health care.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: While the federal government and other states are trying to roll back the right to bodily autonomy and restrict access to comprehensive, inclusive care, a city has taken a stand.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Anyone, no matter who they are, where they come from, or how much they can afford, should be able to get high-quality, nonjudgmental care for the full range of reproductive health services they may need.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The legislation before us today builds on that strong foundation.

chapters.summary: Schulman presents Intro 200-A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, which would require DOHMH to develop materials about obtaining doula care. She says doulas improve birth outcomes, especially for women of color, and should help shape how the city supports their work.
chapters.title: Schulman presents Intro 200-A on doula care resources

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 200-A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, would require DOHMH to develop materials about options for obtaining doula care.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Doulas play a vital role in improving birth outcomes, especially for women of color.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This bill would be...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: make sure their voices shape how the city supports their work.

chapters.summary: Schulman presents Intro 211-A, sponsored by Councilmember Shahana Hanif, requiring DOHMH to run a public education and outreach campaign on fertility treatment. The campaign would explain insurance and Medicaid coverage, helping lower-income New Yorkers make informed family-building decisions.
chapters.title: Schulman presents Intro 211-A on fertility treatment outreach

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 211-A, sponsored by Councilmember Shahana Hanif, would require DOHMH to run a public education and outreach campaign on fertility treatment.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The campaign would cover, among other topics, which fertility treatment services are covered by insurance and what Medicaid covers in New York.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Many New Yorkers, especially those with lower incomes, don't know how accessible fertility care can be for them.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This bill would help them make informed decisions about building their families.

chapters.summary: Schulman notes the committee will vote on three state-directed resolutions and presents Res 108-A, sponsored by Councilmember Murano. The resolution calls on the state legislature to pass and the governor to sign S-5262/A-3051, creating a refundable tax credit for up to three cycles of IVF not covered by insurance.
chapters.title: Schulman presents Res 108-A on IVF tax credit

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We also are going to vote on three resolutions calling on the state to act.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Proposed Resolution 108-A, sponsored by Councilmember Murano, calls on the state legislature to pass and the governor to sign S-

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: 5262 and A3051, which would create a refundable tax credit for up to three cycles of in vitro fertilization not covered by insurance.

chapters.summary: Schulman presents Res 447, sponsored by Councilmember Kayla Santasoso, calling on the state to ensure insurance companies cover preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies. She notes the resolution is part of the committee's reproductive health package.
chapters.title: Schulman presents Res 447 on PGT-A insurance coverage

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Resolution 447, sponsored by Councilmember Kayla Santasoso, calls on the state to make sure insurance companies cover the cost of PGT.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: A testing.

chapters.summary: Schulman presents Res 89-A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, calling on the state to pass S-2058/A-9175. The bill would require every SUNY and CUNY institution to have at least one vending machine selling emergency contraception.
chapters.title: Schulman presents Res 89-A on emergency contraception vending machines

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Proposed Resolution 89-A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer, I'm sorry,

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, calls on the state legislature to pass and the governor to sign S-2058-A9175, which would require every SUNY and CUNY institution

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: to have at least one vending machine that sells emergency contraception.

chapters.summary: Schulman says the legislative package will strengthen access to reproductive and maternal health care regardless of income. She says the council is committed to a healthier New York City where families feel empowered to make informed decisions.
chapters.title: Schulman says legislative package will strengthen reproductive and maternal care

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This legislature

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The legislative package will strengthen access to reproductive and maternal health care for everyone, regardless of income.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This council is committed to building a New York City where families are healthier and feel empowered to make informed decisions about their futures.

chapters.summary: Schulman thanks the sponsors and committee staff Chris Pepe, Josh Newman, Elizabeth Arts, and Valeria Lazario-Rodriguez, as well as her team Jonathan Boucher, Kevin McAleer, and Sammy New. She then turns the floor over to Councilmember Gutierrez for a statement.
chapters.title: Schulman thanks sponsors, committee staff, and her team

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I want to thank the sponsors for their leadership on the legislation we're considering today, as well as the committee staff, Chris Pepe, Josh Newman, Elizabeth Arts, and Valeria Lazario-Rodriguez for their hard work in preparing for this vote.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I also want to thank my team, Jonathan Boucher, Kevin McAleer, and Sammy New.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Now I will turn it over to Councilmember Gutierrez to make a statement in support of her.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez thanks Chair Schulman for her support and says she is championing two measures to advance maternal and reproductive rights. She introduces Intro 200 and Res 89-A as the items she will discuss.
chapters.title: Council Member Gutierrez thanks Chair Schulman and introduces her bills

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: First, I just want to thank Chair Shulman, who's been completely supportive and unwavering in all legislation that this council tries to push that's forward-thinking and protecting women and women of color.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So thank you so much, Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Today we're voting on two pieces of legislation that I've been really proud to champion, which further maternal and reproductive rights in New York City.

chapters.summary: Gutierrez says Intro 200 strengthens the role of doulas in hospitals and ensures respectful, consistent, informed care for birthing people. She says doulas lower preterm births and C-sections, improve birth experiences, and helped her during both of her own births.
chapters.title: Gutierrez explains Intro 200-A doula protections and benefits

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: The first, Intro 200, strengthens the role of doulas in hospitals and ensures that they are respected and that the people that are there to give birth receive respectful, consistent, and informed care across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Having doulas present lowers preterm birth, it lowers the need for a C-section, and increases positive birth experiences.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm someone that benefited from having a doula in the room with both of my children, and I can say that that attributed to the positive experiences that I had.

chapters.summary: Gutierrez says more New Yorkers use doulas, but doulas are often disrespected, kicked out of rooms, ignored, or told they are not medical staff. She argues a clear doula bill of rights will enforce state-protected rights and advance a more equitable maternal health system.
chapters.title: Gutierrez describes disrespect doulas face and need for bill of rights

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And more and more New Yorkers are utilizing this invaluable service of doulas, but doulas are often

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: not respected in these hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Sometimes they're kicked out of rooms.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: They're ignored.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: They are told that they are not part of the medical staff.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And so this can be extremely negatively and emotional detrimental to the birthing client.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: They have state protected rights, but so often they're not enforced.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And by creating a clear doula bill of rights, we strengthen doula protections.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: By strengthening those protections, we can strengthen birth outcomes across the city and advance a more equitable maternal health system.

chapters.summary: Gutierrez presents Res 89-A, which calls on the state to require SUNY and CUNY institutions to install at least one vending machine selling emergency contraception. She says machines would be in accessible locations with extended hours, providing a confidential, low-barrier option alongside student health services.
chapters.title: Gutierrez presents Res 89-A on campus emergency contraception vending

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And my second piece of legislation, Reso 89A, calls on the state to require each SUNY, of which I am a proud alum, and CUNY institution to install at least one vending machine that makes emergency contraception available for purchase.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Machines would be placed in accessible locations with extended hours, providing a confidential and low barrier option that complements existing student health services.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: This approach builds on proven models already in use at campuses in New York and across the country.

chapters.summary: Gutierrez says students face barriers including limited clinic hours, inconsistent campus policies, and uneven pharmacy availability. She notes Black, Hispanic, and uninsured students are at higher risk of unintended pregnancy, so on-campus access supports health, autonomy, and academic success.
chapters.title: Gutierrez cites barriers and equity concerns for student contraception access

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Students across New York face significant barriers to accessing emergency contraception, including limited clinic hours, inconsistent campus policies, and uneven availability at pharmacies.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Young adults, particularly Black, Hispanic, and uninsured students who make up a large share of SUNY and CUNY enrollment, are at a higher risk for unintended pregnancy and more likely to need contraceptive services.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Improving on-campus access supports students'health, autonomy, and ability to remain enrolled and succeed academically.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And thank you to the lead staff that helped put this all together.

chapters.summary: Schulman thanks Gutierrez, acknowledges the arrival of Council Members Felder, Marte, Narcisse, De La Rosa, Epstein, and Wilson, and announces she will read a statement from Councilmember Santa Soso on Resolution 447. The statement is read into the record by Schulman.
chapters.title: Schulman acknowledges members and turns to Res 447 statement

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Before we move on, I want to acknowledge that we've been joined by council members.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Felder, Marte, Norcis, De La Rosa, Epstein, and Wilson.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I am now going to read a statement from Councilmember Santa Soso on Resolution No.

chapters.summary: In a statement read by Schulman, Councilmember Santa Soso thanks Chair Shulman and staff Julia Goldsmith-Pinkham and Christy Dwyer for drafting Res 447. The resolution calls on the state to expand insurance coverage of PGT-A testing for those pursuing IVF.
chapters.title: Santa Soso statement thanks staff and introduces Res 447

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I want to start by offering my gratitude to Chair Shulman for including this item on the agenda for today's Health Committee meeting.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I also want to thank Julia Goldsmith-Pinkham and Christy Dwyer for their help drafting this resolution.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Reso 447 calls on our colleagues in the state government to expand insurance coverage of essential PGTA testing and give those striving to have children their best chance at success.

chapters.summary: The statement says gaps in insurance coverage force people to take unnecessary and costly risks during IVF. It explains that PGT-A screens for euploid embryos, reduces miscarriage and time to pregnancy, and can be cost-saving by shortening IVF treatment.
chapters.title: Santa Soso statement explains PGT-A benefits and cost savings

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Despite all of the progress we have made in helping families realize their dream of having children, gaps in insurance coverage are still forcing people to take unnecessary and costly risks when...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Pursuing IVF treatments.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: PGT is an essential screening tool that can significantly reduce the rate of miscarriage and time to pregnancy by screening for euploid embryos.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This kind of testing reduces the physical, emotional, and financial toll that IVF can have on would-be parents by increasing the rate of success and decreasing the chances of miscarriage.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Because this testing can reduce the length of time IVF is needed, it can be seen as a cost-saving measure.

chapters.summary: The statement says insurance companies covering city employees still treat PGT-A as non-essential, forcing would-be parents to skip testing or pay out of pocket. It calls on the state to require coverage for all city employees, arguing that will make IVF more successful and less costly.
chapters.title: Santa Soso statement urges state to cover PGT-A for city employees

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Despite all of this, insurance companies covering city employees still view PGT testing as non-essential, forcing would-be parents to decide to skip testing or pay costly fees out of pocket.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This places unnecessary burdens on families and often time increases the overall cost of IVF for everyone involved, including

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: including the insurance companies themselves.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We are calling on the state to pass legislation to ensure PGT.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: A testing is covered for all city employees.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This will encourage more people to do PGT-A tests, making IVF procedures more successful and less costly.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you to all of my colleagues on the Health Committee for taking the time to consider this critical piece of legislation.

chapters.summary: Schulman thanks colleagues and calls for a vote on Intros 200-A and 211-A and Resos 89-A, 108-A, and 447. Committee Clerk Ben Jacobs then announces the roll call on those items.
chapters.title: Schulman calls for vote; Committee Clerk begins roll call

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And now I call for a vote.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ben Jacobs, Committee Clerk, the City Council Committee on Health.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This is the roll call vote on introductions 200A, 211A, and resolutions 89A, 108A, and 447.

chapters.title: Committee Clerk conducts roll call on reproductive health package

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Wilson.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Council Member Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I vote aye on all, with the exception of Resolution 89A, on which I vote no.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember De La Rosa.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Aye on all and congrats.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Felder.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I vote yes on all, and congratulations to the sponsors.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And Councilmember Areola.

chapters.summary: The clerk reports eight affirmative votes, none negative, and no abstentions on all items except Resolution 89-A. This approves Intros 200-A and 211-A and Resos 108-A and 447.
chapters.title: Clerk announces approval of all items except Res 89-A

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay, that is a vote of eight in the affirmative, none in the negative, and no abstentions on all items except for Resolution 89.

chapters.title: Clerk announces Res 89-A passes 7-1 and all items adopted

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And on Resolution 89, it's seven in the affirmative, one in the negative, and no abstentions.

utterances.text: But all items are adopted.

chapters.title: Chair Schulman acknowledges Gennaro and adjourns Health Committee hearing

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I just I also want to acknowledge that Councilmember Gennaro, I mean, he voted before I acknowledged that he was here because he came late, but that he's here.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And also.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman

summary: The Committee on Health held a vote on two local laws and three resolutions focused on reproductive and maternal health.

Bills included Intro 200-A on doula care resources and Intro 211-A on fertility treatment outreach; resolutions addressed IVF tax credits, PGT-A coverage, and emergency contraception vending machines.
All items were adopted, with Resolution 89-A passing 7-1 after Council Member Gennaro voted no.
